s.d: ὀπτάνω [in LXX: [[1-kings 8 8|3Ki.8:8]] (רָאָה ni.), Tob.12:19 * ;] late present as from ὤφθην (= ὁράω); mid., ὀπτάνομαι, to allow oneself to be seen, to appear. with dative, [[acts 1 3|Act.1:3.]] (For exx. from π., see Deiss., LAE, 79, 2526; MM, ii, xviii.) † (AS)

ὀπτασία, -ας, ἡ (ὀπτάζομαι, [[numbers 14 14|Num.14:14]]* = ὀπτάνομαι), later form of ὄψις, [in LXX: [[malachi 3 2|Mal.3:2]] (רָאָה ni.), Da TH [[daniel 9 23|Dan.9:23 10:1, 7-8 10:16]] (מַרְאֶה, מַרְאָה LXX, ὅραμα, -σις), [[esther 4 7|Est.4:7]], Sir.43:2, 16 * ;] 1. an appearing, coming into view (Ma, Es, Sir, ll. with). 2. a vision: [[luke 1 22|Luk.1:22 24:23]], [[acts 26 19|Act.26:19]], [[2-corinthians 12 1|2Co.12:1]] (Da, ll. with, also in MGr.).† (AS)
ὀπτός, -ή, -όν [in LXX: [[exodus 12 8|Exo.12:8-9]] (צָלִי) * ;] roasted, boiled [[luke 24 42|Luk.24:42.]]† (AS)

ὀπώρα, -ας, ἡ [in LXX: [[jeremiah 48 32|Jer.48:32 40:10, 12]] (קַיִץ) * ;] 1. late summer, early autumn (the time between the risings of Sirius and Arcturus, i.e. late July, all August and early September). 2. By meton. (as being fruit-time), ripe fruits [[revelation 18 14|Rev.18:14]] (cf. φθινοπωρινά, Ju 12).† (AS)

ὅπως I. Relat. adv. of manner, as, how: with indic., [[luke 24 20|Luk.24:20.]] II. Conj., with subjc. (in cl. also with opt., indic.: so in [[matthew 26 59|Mat.26:59]], LT, Tr.), in order that, to the end that, that; 1. final, denoting purpose or design (in which the original idea of modality has been merged): after pres., [[matthew 6 2|Mat.6:2]], al.; pf., [[acts 9 17|Act.9:17]], al.; impf., [[acts 9 24|Act.9:24;]] aor., [[acts 9 2|Act.9:2]], al.; plpf., [[john 11 57|Jhn.11:57;]] fut., [[matthew 23 35|Mat.23:35;]] imperat., [[matthew 2 8|Mat.2:8]], al.; ὅ. μή (M, Pr., 185), [[matthew 6 18|Mat.6:18]], [[luke 16 26|Luk.16:26]], [[acts 20 16|Act.20:16]], [[1-corinthians 1 29|1Co.1:29]]; ὅ. πληρωθῇ, [[matthew 2 23|Mat.2:23 8:17 13:35]]; ὅ. ἄν (B1., § 65, 2; WM, § 42, 5), [[luke 2 35|Luk.2:35]], [[acts 3 19|Act.3:19 15:17]], [[romans 3 4|Rom.3:4]] (cf. [[genesis 12 13|Gen.12:13]], [[psalms 59 7|Psa.59:7]]. 1Mac 1032, al.). 2. After verbs of asking, exhorting, etc.: [[matthew 9 38|Mat.9:38]], [[luke 7 3|Luk.7:3]], [[james 5 16|Jas.5:16]], al. (in late writers its place is often taken by the correl. πῶς, which see) (AS)

ὅραμα, -τος, τό (ὁράω), [in LXX for חָזוֹן, מַרְאֶה, etc. ;] that which is seen; (a) a sight, spectacle: [[matthew 17 9|Mat.17:9]], [[acts 7 31|Act.7:31]]; (b) an appearance, vision: [[acts 9 10|Act.9:10, 12]] (Rec.) [[acts 10 3|Act.10:3, 17 10:19 11:5 12:9 16:9-10 18:9]] (cf. ὀπτασία).† (AS)

ὅρασις, -εως, ἡ (ὁράω) [in LXX chiefly for מַרְאֶה, חָזוֹן and cognate forms ;] 1. in Arist. and later writers, the act of seeing, the sense of sight, and by meton., pl., the eyes. 2. appearance ([[numbers 24 4|Num.24:4]], [[ezekiel 1 5|Eze.1:5]], Sir.41:20, al.): [[revelation 4 3|Rev.4:3]]. 3. = ὅραμα, a vision: [[acts 2 17|Act.2:17]] (LXX), [[revelation 9 17|Rev.9:17.]]† (AS)
ὁρατός, -ή, -όν (ὁράω) visible: τὰ ὁ., [[colossians 1 16|Col.1:16.]]† (AS)

ὁράω, -ῶ, [in LXX chiefly for ראה, also for חזה, etc. ;] in "durative" sense (hence aor. act., εἶδον, pass., ὤφθην, fut., ὄψομαι, from different roots; see M, Pr., 110f.), to see (in colloq. even the present is rare, its place being generally taken by θεωρέω, see BL, §24). 1. Of bodily vision, to see, perceive, behold: absol., [[mark 6 38|Mrk.6:38]], al.; ἔρχου καὶ ἴδε, [[john 1 46|Jhn.1:46]], al.; before ὅτι, [[mark 2 16|Mrk.2:16]], al.; with accusative, [[matthew 2 2|Mat.2:2]], [[mark 1 10|Mrk.1:10 16:7]], [[galatians 1 19|Gal.1:19]], al.; θεόν, [[john 1 18|Jhn.1:18]], [[1-john 4 20|1Jn.4:20]], al. 2. to see with the mind, perceive, discern: absol, [[romans 15 21|Rom.15:21;]] with accusative of thing(s), [[matthew 9 2|Mat.9:2 27:54]], [[acts 8 23|Act.8:23]], [[colossians 2 18|Col.2:18]], al. 3. to see, take heed, beware: ὅρα μή, with aor. subjc., [[matthew 8 4|Mat.8:4 18:10]], [[mark 1 44|Mrk.1:44]], [[1-thessalonians 5 15|1Th.5:15]]; id., sc. μὴ ποήσῃς, [[revelation 19 10|Rev.19:10 22:9]] (Bl., §81, 1); before imperat. [[matthew 9 30|Mat.9:30 16:6]], [[mark 8 15|Mrk.8:15]] 4. to experience: τ. θάνατον, [[luke 2 26|Luk.2:26]], [[hebrews 11 5|Heb.11:5]]; ζωήν, [[john 3 36|Jhn.3:36;]] τ. διαφθοράν, [[acts 2 27|Act.2:27.]] 5. to visit: with accusative of person(s), [[luke 8 20|Luk.8:20]], [[john 12 21|Jhn.12:21]], [[romans 1 11|Rom.1:11]], al.; with accusative loc, [[acts 19 21|Act.19:21.]] 6. to see to, care for: [[matthew 27 4|Mat.27:4]], [[acts 18 15|Act.18:15]] (cf. ἀφ-, καθ-, προ-, συν-οράω). SYN.: see: βλέπω. (AS)

ὁράω, -ῶ, [in LXX chiefly for ראה, also for חזה, etc. ;] in "durative" sense (hence aor. act., εἶδον, pass., ὤφθην, fut., ὄψομαι, from different roots; see M, Pr., 110f.), to see (in colloq. even the present is rare, its place being generally taken by θεωρέω, see BL, §24). 1. Of bodily vision, to see, perceive, behold: absol., [[mark 6 38|Mrk.6:38]], al.; ἔρχου καὶ ἴδε, [[john 1 46|Jhn.1:46]], al.; before ὅτι, [[mark 2 16|Mrk.2:16]], al.; with accusative, [[matthew 2 2|Mat.2:2]], [[mark 1 10|Mrk.1:10 16:7]], [[galatians 1 19|Gal.1:19]], al.; θεόν, [[john 1 18|Jhn.1:18]], [[1-john 4 20|1Jn.4:20]], al. 2. to see with the mind, perceive, discern: absol, [[romans 15 21|Rom.15:21;]] with accusative of thing(s), [[matthew 9 2|Mat.9:2 27:54]], [[acts 8 23|Act.8:23]], [[colossians 2 18|Col.2:18]], al. 3. to see, take heed, beware: ὅρα μή, with aor. subjc., [[matthew 8 4|Mat.8:4 18:10]], [[mark 1 44|Mrk.1:44]], [[1-thessalonians 5 15|1Th.5:15]]; id., sc. μὴ ποήσῃς, [[revelation 19 10|Rev.19:10 22:9]] (Bl., §81, 1); before imperat. [[matthew 9 30|Mat.9:30 16:6]], [[mark 8 15|Mrk.8:15]] 4. to experience: τ. θάνατον, [[luke 2 26|Luk.2:26]], [[hebrews 11 5|Heb.11:5]]; ζωήν, [[john 3 36|Jhn.3:36;]] τ. διαφθοράν, [[acts 2 27|Act.2:27.]] 5. to visit: with accusative of person(s), [[luke 8 20|Luk.8:20]], [[john 12 21|Jhn.12:21]], [[romans 1 11|Rom.1:11]], al.; with accusative loc, [[acts 19 21|Act.19:21.]] 6. to see to, care for: [[matthew 27 4|Mat.27:4]], [[acts 18 15|Act.18:15]] (cf. ἀφ-, καθ-, προ-, συν-οράω). SYN.: see: βλέπω. (AS)

ὀργή, -ῆς, ἡ [in LXX chiefly for אַף, also for חָרוֹן, חֵמָה, קָצַף, etc. ;] 1 1, impulse, propensity, disposition. 2. anger, wrath; (a) of men: [[mark 3 5|Mrk.3:5]], [[ephesians 4 31|Eph.4:31]], [[colossians 3 8|Col.3:8]], [[1-timothy 2 8|1Ti.2:8]], [[james 1 19|Jas.1:19-20]]; (b) of God; α that reaction of the divine nature against sin which in anthropomorphic language is called anger: [[romans 1 18|Rom.1:18 9:22 12:19]], (ICC, in l), [[1-thessalonians 1 10|1Th.1:10 2:16]], [[hebrews 3 11|Heb.3:11 4:3]]" (LXX) [[revelation 14 10|Rev.14:10 16:19 19:15]]; β of the effect of God's anger: [[matthew 3 7|Mat.3:7]], [[luke 3 7|Luk.3:7 21:23]], [[john 3 36|Jhn.3:36]], [[romans 2 5|Rom.2:5, 8 3:5 4:15 5:9 13:4-5]] [[ephesians 5 6|Eph.5:6]], [[colossians 3 6|Col.3:6]], [[1-thessalonians 5 9|1Th.5:9]], [[james 1 20|Jas.1:20]], [[revelation 6 16|Rev.6:16-17 11:18]]; σκεύη ὀργῆς, [[romans 9 22|Rom.9:22;]] τέκνα ὀργῆς, [[ephesians 2 3|Eph.2:3.]]† SYN.: see: θυμός (AS)

ὀργίζω (ὀργή), [in LXX chiefly for חָרָה, also for קָצַף, etc. ;] to make angry, provoke to anger; in cl. most frequently in pass., and so always in NT, to be provoked to anger, be angry: absol., [[matthew 18 34|Mat.18:34 22:7]], [[luke 14 21|Luk.14:21 15:28]], [[ephesians 4 26|Eph.4:26]]" (LXX), [[revelation 11 18|Rev.11:18;]] with dative, [[matthew 5 22|Mat.5:22;]] before ἐπί, with dative (3Ki.11:9, al.), [[revelation 12 17|Rev.12:17]] (cf. παρ-ὀργίζω).† (AS)
ὀργίλος, -η, -ον (ὀργή), [in LXX: [[proverbs 22 24|Pro.22:24 29:22]] (חֵמָה), etc. ;] inclined to anger, passionate: [[titus 1 7|Tit.1:7.]]† (AS)
ὀργυιά, -ᾶς, ἡ (ὀρέγω), the length of the outstretched arms, a fathom: [[acts 27 28|Act.27:28.]]† (AS)

ὀρέγω [in Sm.: [[job 8 20|Job.8:20]], [[ezekiel 16 49|Eze.16:49]] * ;] to reach, stretch out; pass. and mid., to stretch oneself out, reach forth; metaphorically, to reach after, grasp at, aspire to: with genitive of thing(s), [[1-timothy 3 1|1Ti.3:1]], [[hebrews 11 16|Heb.11:16]]; φιλαργυρίας (see Ellic. and CGT, in l), [[1-timothy 6 10|1Ti.6:10.]]† SYN.: ἐπιθυμέω, to desire (which see) (AS)
ὀρεινός (WH, ὀριν-; see MM, xviii,) -ή, -όν (ὄρος), mountainous, hilly; ἡ ὀ. (sc. χώρα), the hill-country (LXX for הַר): [[luke 1 39|Luk.1:39, 65]] † (AS)

ὄρεξις, -εως, ἡ (ὀρέγομαι), [in LXX Wis.14:2 15:5 16:2-3, Sir.18:30 23:6, 4Ma.1:33 4Mac 1:35 * ;] the most general ward for all kinds of desire, longing, appetite: of lust, [[romans 1 27|Rom.1:27]] SYN.: see: πάθος (AS)
ὀρθοποδέω, -ῶ (ὀρθό-πους, going straight), = cl. εὐθυπορέω, to walk straight: metaphorically, [[galatians 2 14|Gal.2:14]] (not elsewhere).† (AS)

ὀρθός, -ή, -όν [in LXX chiefly for יָשָׁר ;] straight; (a) in height, straight, upright: [[acts 14 10|Act.14:10;]] (b) in line, straight, direct: figuratively, [[hebrews 12 13|Heb.12:13]] (LXX).† (AS)

ὀρθοτομέω, -ῶ (- ὀρθός, τέμνω), [in LXX: [[proverbs 3 6|Pro.3:6 11:6]] (יָשַׁר pi.)* ;] to cut straight, as a road (τ. ὁδούς, figuratively, Pr, ll with). Metaphorical, τ. λόγον τ. ἀληθείας, [[2-timothy 2 15|2Ti.2:15]] (V. Ellic. and CGT, in l; not found elsewhere).† (AS)

ὀρθρίζω (ὄρθρος), [in LXX chiefly for שָׁכַם hi., [[genesis 19 2|Gen.19:2]], al.; also for שָׁחַר pi., [[psalms 63 1|Psa.63:1]], al., etc. ;] = cl. poët., ὀρθρεύω, to rise early: before πρός, with accusative of person(s) (as Ps, l.with, al.), [[luke 21 38|Luk.21:38]] (see Thumb, Hellen., 123).† (AS)
ὀρθρινός, -ή, -όν (ὄρθρος), [in LXX: [[hosea 6 4|Hos.6:4 13:3]] (שָׁכַם hi.), [[haggai 2 14|Hag.2:14]], Wis.11:22 * ;] late form of ὄρθριος (which see), early: [[luke 24 22|Luk.24:22.]]† (AS)

ὄρθριος, -α, -ον (ὄρθρος), [in LXX: [[1-kings 28 14|1Ki.28:14]], [[job 29 7|Job.29:7, 1-25]]; 3Ma.5:10 3Mac 5:23 * ;] early, in the early morning: [[luke 24 22|Luk.24:22]], Rec. (see: ὀρθρινός).† (AS)

ὄρθρος, -ου, ὁ [in LXX for שַׁחַר, בֹּקֶר, etc. ;] daybreak, dawn: ὄρθρου βαθέως (M, Pr., 73), at early dawn, [[luke 24 1|Luk.24:1;]] ὄρθρου, [[john 8 2|Jhn.8:2;]] ὑπὸ τὸν ὄ., [[acts 5 21|Act.5:21]] (cf. MM, xviii).† (AS)
όρθῶς adv. (ἀρθός), rightly: [[mark 7 35|Mrk.7:35]], [[luke 7 43|Luk.7:43 10:28 20:21]].† (AS)

ὁρίζω (ὅρος, a boundary), [in LXX for אָסַר, גְּבוּל, etc. ;] 1. to separate, mark off by boundaries (so [[numbers 34 6|Num.34:6]], [[john 13 27|Jhn.13:27]]). 2. to determine, appoint, designate: of time, with accusative, [[acts 17 26|Act.17:26]], [[hebrews 4 7|Heb.4:7]]; with accusative of person(s), [[acts 17 31|Act.17:31;]] with inf., [[acts 11 29|Act.11:29;]] pass., [[luke 22 22|Luk.22:22]], [[acts 2 23|Act.2:23 10:42]], [[romans 1 4|Rom.1:4]] (cf. ὀφ-, ἀπο- δι-, τρο-ορίζω),† (AS)

ὅριον, -ου, τό (ὅρος, a boundary), [in LXX chiefly for גְּבוּל ;] a boundary, bound; chiefly in pl., and so always in NT: [[matthew 2 16|Mat.2:16 4:13 8:34 15:22, 39 19:1]], [[mark 5 17|Mrk.5:17 7:24, 31 10:1]], [[acts 13 50|Act.13:50]].† (AS)

ὁρκίζω (ὅρκος), [in LXX: [[genesis 24 37|Gen.24:37]], al. (שָׁבַע hi.) ;] 1. to make one swear (Xen., Polyb., a1.). 2. to adjure: with dupl. accusative, [[mark 5 7|Mrk.5:7]], [[acts 19 13|Act.19:13]] (cf. ἐν-, ἐξ-ορκίζω).† (AS)

ὅρκος, -ου, ὁ [in LXX chiefly for שֶׁוַע, שִׁבְעָה and cogn. forms ;] an oath: [[matthew 14 7|Mat.14:7 26:72]], [[luke 1 73|Luk.1:73]], [[acts 2 30|Act.2:30]], [[hebrews 6 16|Heb.6:16-17]], [[james 5 12|Jas.5:12]]; p1., [[matthew 5 33|Mat.5:33]] (LXX) [[matthew 14 9|Mat.14:9]], [[mark 6 26|Mrk.6:26]].† (AS)

ὁρκωμοσία, -ας, ἡ (ὅρκος, ὄμνυμι; by metapl. for τὰ ὁρκωμόσια, asseverations on oath; see MM, xviii), [in LXX: [[ezekiel 17 18|Eze.17:18-19]] (עָלָה) 1Es 9:93* ;] affirmation on oath, an oath: [[hebrews 7 20|Heb.7:20-21, 28]].† (AS)

ὁρμάω, -ῶ (ὁρμή), [in LXX for שׁוּב, etc. ;] 1. causal, to set in motion, urge on. 2. Intrans., to hasten on, rush: before εἰς, [[matthew 8 32|Mat.8:32]], [[mark 5 13|Mrk.5:13]], [[luke 8 33|Luk.8:33]], [[acts 19 29|Act.19:29]]; ἐπί, with accusative, [[acts 7 57|Act.7:57.]]† (AS)
ὁρμή, -ῆς, ἡ [in LXX: [[proverbs 3 25|Pro.3:25]] (שׁוֹא), etc. ;] 1. a violent movement, impulse: [[james 3 4|Jas.3:4;]] 2. a hostile movement, onset, assault. [[acts 14 5|Act.14:5.]]† (AS)
ὅρμημα, -τος, τό (ὁρμάω) [in LXX: [[hosea 5 10|Hos.5:10]], [[amos 1 11|Amo.1:11]] (עֶבְרָה), etc. ;] a rush: [[revelation 18 21|Rev.18:21.]]† (AS)
ὄρνεον, -ου, τό = ὄρνις, [in LXX chiefly for צִפּוֹר ;] a bird: [[revelation 18 2|Rev.18:2 19:17, 21]] (Hom., al.).† (AS)
ὄρνις, -ιθος, ὁ, ἡ [in LXX: ὄ. ἐκλεκταί, I2Ki.3:1 4:23 ([[1-kings 5 3|3Ki.5:3]]) (בַּרְבֻּר)* ;] a bird; specif., a cock, a hen: [[matthew 23 3|Mat.23:3]], [[luke 13 34|Luk.13:34]] (WH).† (AS)
ὁροθεσία, -ας, ἡ (ὅρος, a boundary, + τίθημι) a setting of boundaries; in pl., bounds; [[acts 17 26|Act.17:26.]]† (AS)

ὄρος, -ους, τό [in LXX chiefly, and very freq., for הַר ;] a mountain: [[matthew 4 8|Mat.4:8 17:1]], [[mark 9 2|Mrk.9:2]], [[john 4 20|Jhn.4:20]], [[2-peter 1 18|2Pe.1:18]], al.; opposite to βουνός, [[luke 3 5|Luk.3:5]] (LXX); ὄ. τ. ἐλαιῶν, [[matthew 21 1|Mat.21:1 24:3]], al. (see: ἐ.); ὄ. Σιών (Σ., prob. in gem appos.), [[hebrews 12 22|Heb.12:22]], [[revelation 14 1|Rev.14:1]]; ὄ. Σινά, [[acts 7 30|Act.7:30, 38]] [[galatians 4 24|Gal.4:24-25]]; τὸ ὄ., of the hill district as distinct from the lowlands, esp. the hills above the Sea of Galilee, [[matthew 5 1|Mat.5:1 8:1]], [[mark 3 13|Mrk.3:13 6:46]], al.; τὰ ὄ., [[matthew 18 12|Mat.18:12]], [[mark 5 5|Mrk.5:5]], [[hebrews 11 38|Heb.11:38]], [[revelation 6 14|Rev.6:14]], al.; proverbially (cf. Rabbinic, הדים עקר), of overcoming difficulties, accomplishing marvels, ὄρη μεθιστάνειν, [[1-corinthians 13 2|1Co.13:2]], cf. [[matthew 17 20|Mat.17:20 21:21]], [[mark 11 23|Mrk.11:23]] (AS)

ὀρύσσω [in LXX chiefly for חָפַר also for כָּרָה, etc. ;] to dig: with accusative, ληνόν, [[matthew 21 33|Mat.21:33;]] ὁπολήνιον, [[mark 12 1|Mrk.12:1;]] γῆν, [[matthew 25 18|Mat.25:18]] (cf. δι-, ἐξ-ορύσσω).† (AS)

ὀρφανός, -ή, -όν [in LXX for יָתוֹם ;] 1. prop., orphan, fatherless: [[mark 12 40|Mrk.12:40]], WH, mg, [[james 1 27|Jas.1:27.]] 2. In a general sense (as also in cl.; see LS, see word; and cf. MM, xviii), bereft, friendless, desolate: [[john 14 18|Jhn.14:18.]]† (AS)
ὀρχέομαι, -οῦμαι [in LXX for רָקַד, etc. ;] to dance; [[matthew 11 17|Mat.11:17 14:6]], [[mark 6 22|Mrk.6:22]], [[luke 7 32|Luk.7:32]].† (AS)

ὅς, ἥ, ὅ, the postpositive article (ἄρθρον ὑποτακτικόν). I. As demonstr. pron. = οὗτος, ὅδε, this, that, also for αὐτός, chiefly in nom.: ὅς δέ, but he (cf. ἦ δὲ ὅς, frequently in Plat.), [[mark 15 23|Mrk.15:23]], [[john 5 11|Jhn.5:11]]; ὃς μὲν . . . ὃς δέ, the one . . . the other, [[matthew 21 35|Mat.21:35, 22:5, 25:15]], [[luke 23 33|Luk.23:33]], [[acts 27 14|Act.27:14]], [[romans 14 5|Rom.14:5]], [[1-corinthians 11 21|1Co.11:21]], [[2-corinthians 2 18|2Co.2:18]], Ju 22; neut., ὃ μὲν . . . ὃ δέ, the one . . . the other, some . . . some, [[matthew 13 8|Mat.13:8, 23]], [[romans 9 21|Rom.9:21]]; ὃς (ὃ) μὲν . . . (ἄλλος (ἄλλο)) . . . ἕτερος, [[mark 4 4|Mrk.4:4]], [[luke 8 5|Luk.8:5]], [[1-corinthians 12 8|1Co.12:8-10]]; οὓς μέν, absol., [[1-corinthians 12 28|1Co.12:28;]] ὃς μὲν . . . ὁ δέ, [[romans 14 2|Rom.14:2.]] II. As relat. pron., who, which, what, that; 1. agreeing in gender with its antecedent, but differently governed as to case: [[matthew 2 9|Mat.2:9]], [[luke 9 9|Luk.9:9]], [[acts 20 18|Act.20:18]], [[romans 2 29|Rom.2:29]], al. mult. 2. In variation from the common construction; (a) in gender, agreeing with a noun in apposition to the antecedent: [[mark 15 16|Mrk.15:16]], [[galatians 3 16|Gal.3:16]], [[ephesians 6 17|Eph.6:17]], al.; constr. ad sensum: [[john 6 9|Jhn.6:9]], [[colossians 2 19|Col.2:19]], [[1-timothy 3 16|1Ti.3:16]], [[revelation 13 14|Rev.13:14]], al.; (b) in number, constr. ad sensum: [[acts 15 36|Act.15:36]], [[2-peter 3 1|2Pe.3:1]]; (with) in case, by attraction to the case of the antecedent (Bl., §50, 2): [[john 4 18|Jhn.4:18]], [[acts 3 21|Act.3:21]], [[romans 15 18|Rom.15:18]], [[1-corinthians 6 19|1Co.6:19]], [[ephesians 1 8|Eph.1:8]], al. 3. The neut. ὅ with nouns of other gender and with phrases, which thing, which term: [[mark 3 17|Mrk.3:17 12:42]], [[john 1 39|Jhn.1:39]], [[colossians 3 14|Col.3:14]], al.; with a sentence, [[acts 2 32|Act.2:32]], [[galatians 2 10|Gal.2:10]], [[1-john 2 8|1Jn.2:8]], al. 4. With ellipse of a demonstrative (οὗτος or ἐκεῖνος), before or after: before, [[matthew 20 23|Mat.20:23]], [[luke 7 43|Luk.7:43]], [[romans 10 14|Rom.10:14]], al.; after, [[matthew 10 38|Mat.10:38]], [[mark 9 40|Mrk.9:40]], [[john 19 22|Jhn.19:22]], [[romans 2 1|Rom.2:1]] al. 5. Expressing purpose, end or cause: [[matthew 11 10|Mat.11:10]] (who = that he may), [[mark 1 2|Mrk.1:2]], [[hebrews 12 6|Heb.12:6]] al. 6. ὀφειλέτης, -ου, ὁ (ὀφείλω), a debtor: with genitive (of the amount), [[matthew 18 24|Mat.18:24.]] Metaphorical, of obligation or duty in general, with reference to favours received or injury done, etc.: [[matthew 6 12|Mat.6:12]], [[romans 1 14|Rom.1:14 8:12 15:27]], [[galatians 5 3|Gal.5:3]]; of sinners, in relation to God (= Heb. חַיָּב; cf. ὀφειλή, -ῆς, ἡ (ὀφείλω), a debt: [[matthew 18 32|Mat.18:32;]] metaphorically, one's due: [[romans 13 7|Rom.13:7]], [[1-corinthians 7 3|1Co.7:3]] (found also in π.; see Deiss., BS, 221; MM, xviii).† (AS)

ὀφείλημα, -τος, τό (ὀφείλω), [in LXX: [[deuteronomy 24 10|Deu.24:10]] (מַשָּׁאָה), I [[esther 3 20|Est.3:20]], 1Ma.15:8 * ;] that which is owed, a debt: [[romans 4 4|Rom.4:4;]] metaphorically (as Aram. חוֺבָא חוֺב), of sin as a debt, [[matthew 6 12|Mat.6:12.]]† (AS)

ὀφείλω [in LXX: [[deuteronomy 15 2|Deu.15:2]], [[isaiah 24 2|Isa.24:2]] (נָשָׁה), [[ezekiel 18 7|Eze.18:7]] (חוֹב), Wis.12:15, 20, al. ;] to owe, be a debtor: with accusative of thing(s), [[matthew 18 28|Mat.18:28]], [[luke 7 41|Luk.7:41 16:7]], Phm 18; id. with dative of person(s), [[matthew 18 28|Mat.18:28]], [[luke 16 5|Luk.16:5]]. Pass., to be owed, to be due: τ. ὀφειλόμενον, [[matthew 18 30|Mat.18:30, 34]]. Metaphorical: absol. (= Rabbinic חַיָּב; see McNeile, in l), [[matthew 23 16|Mat.23:16, 18]]; with accusative of thing(s) and dative of person(s), [[romans 13 8|Rom.13:8;]] with inf., to be bound or obliged to do (of. Westc., Epp. Jo., 50), [[luke 17 10|Luk.17:10]], [[john 13 14|Jhn.13:14 19:7]], [[acts 17 29|Act.17:29]], [[romans 15 1|Rom.15:1, 27]], [[1-corinthians 5 10|1Co.5:10 7:36 9:10 11:7 11:10]], [[2-corinthians 12 14|2Co.12:14]], [[ephesians 5 28|Eph.5:28]], [[2-thessalonians 1 3|2Th.1:3 2:13]], [[hebrews 2 17|Heb.2:17 5:3, 12]], [[1-john 2 6|1Jn.2:6]] [[john 3 16|Jn 3:16]] [[john 4 11|Jn 4:11]], 3Jn.8; ὤειλον συνίστασθαι, I ought to have been commended, [[2-corinthians 12 11|2Co.12:11.]] In peculiar Aram. sense of having wronged one (see: όφείλημα; but of. also Inscr. ἁμαρτίαν ὀφείίλω, Deiss., BS, 225), with dative of person(s), [[luke 11 4|Luk.11:4]] (cf. προσ-οφίελω).† (AS)

ὄφελον 2 aorist of ὀφείλω, without the augment (see M, Pr., 201n), used to express a fruitless wish; [in LXX (with aor. indic.): [[exodus 16 3|Exo.16:3]] (נָתַן מִי), [[numbers 14 2|Num.14:2]] [[numbers 20 3|Num.20:3]] (לוּא), [[psalms 119 5|Psa.119:5]] (אַחֲלַי), etc. ;] in cl. with an infin. (chiefly poët.), would that: with indic. aor., [[1-corinthians 4 8|1Co.4:8;]] impf., [[2-corinthians 11 1|2Co.11:1]], [[revelation 3 15|Rev.3:15]]; fut., [[galatians 5 12|Gal.5:12]] (a practicable wish, see 131., 206 f., 220. The construction with indic. is only found in late writers.)† (AS)
ὄφελος, -ονς, τό (ὀφέλλω, to increase) [in LXX: [[job 15 3|Job.15:3]] (יָעַל hi.)* ;] advantage, help: [[1-corinthians 15 32|1Co.15:32]], [[james 2 14|Jas.2:14, 16]].† (AS)
ὀφθαλμο-δουλία (Rec. -εία), -ας, ἡ (ὀφθαλμός, δοῦλος), eye-service: [[ephesians 6 6|Eph.6:6]], [[colossians 3 22|Col.3:22]] (not found elsewhere).† (AS)

ὀφθαλμός, -οῦ, ὁ, [in LXX chiefly for עַיִן ;] the eye (as in cl., chiefly pl.): [[matthew 5 38|Mat.5:38]], [[mark 9 47|Mrk.9:47]], [[luke 6 41|Luk.6:41]], [[john 9 6|Jhn.9:6]], al.; τοὺς ὀ. ἐξορύθσσειν (figuratively), [[galatians 4 15|Gal.4:15;]] ἐπᾶραι, [[luke 6 20|Luk.6:20]], [[john 6 5|Jhn.6:5]]; ἀνοῖξα, [[acts 9 40|Act.9:40;]] id., of restoring sight, [[matthew 20 33|Mat.20:33]], [[john 9 10|Jhn.9:10]], al.; ἐν ῥιπῇ ὀφθαλμοῦ, [[1-corinthians 15 52|1Co.15:52;]] by anthropom., of God, [[hebrews 4 13|Heb.4:13]], [[1-peter 3 12|1Pe.3:12]]; pleonastically (cf. Thackeray, Gr., 42f.), εἶδον οἱ ὀ. μοθ, [[luke 2 30|Luk.2:30]] (similarly, [[luke 4 20|ib. 4:20 10:23]], [[john 12 40|Jhn.12:40]], [[1-corinthians 2 9|1Co.2:9]], [[1-john 1 1|1Jn.1:1]], [[revelation 1 7|Rev.1:7]]). Metaphorical (as otherwise in cl.; see LS, see word); (a) of ethical qualities: ὀ. πονηρός (meton., for envy; cf. Heb. עַיִן רַע, [[proverbs 28 22|Pro.28:22;]] cf. Sir.14:10 34:13), [[matthew 6 22|Mat.6:22, 23]] [[mark 7 22|Mrk.7:22]], [[luke 11 34|Luk.11:34]]; ἁπλοῦς, [[matthew 6 22|Mat.6:22]], [[luke 11 34|Luk.11:34]]; ἐπιθυμία (which see) ὀφθαλμῶν (cf. [[ecclesiastes 4 8|Ecc.4:8]], Sir.14:9), [[1-john 2 16|1Jn.2:16]]; ὀ. μεστοὶ μοιχαλἰδος, [[2-peter 2 14|2Pe.2:14;]] (b) of mental vision: [[matthew 13 15|Mat.13:15]], [[mark 8 18|Mrk.8:18]], [[luke 19 42|Luk.19:42]], [[john 12 40|Jhn.12:40]], [[romans 11 8|Rom.11:8]], [[galatians 3 1|Gal.3:1]], [[ephesians 1 18|Eph.1:18]], al.; ἐν ὀφθαλμοῖς before genitive (on the absence of the art., seeBl, §46, 9.II; M, Pr., 81), [[matthew 21 42|Mat.21:42]], [[mark 12 11|Mrk.12:11]]. (AS)

ὄφις, -εως, ὁ [in LXX chiefly for נָחָשׁ ;] a serpent, snake: [[matthew 7 10|Mat.7:10]] [[mark 16 18|Mrk.16:18]], [[luke 10 19|Luk.10:19 11:11]], [[john 3 14|Jhn.3:14]], [[1-corinthians 10 9|1Co.10:9]], [[revelation 9 19|Rev.9:19]]; as typical of wisdom and cunning, [[matthew 10 16|Mat.10:16 23:23]], [[2-corinthians 11 3|2Co.11:3]] (cf. [[genesis 31 1|Gen.31:1-55]]); of Satan (cf. [[genesis 3 1|Gen.3:1]], Wis.2:23-24, 4Ma.18:8), [[revelation 12 9|Rev.12:9, 14 12:11 20:2]].† (AS)
ὀφρύς -ύος, ἡ [in LXX: [[leviticus 14 9|Lev.14:9]] (עַיִן גַב) * ;] an eyebrow, the brow of a hill: [[luke 4 29|Luk.4:29.]]† (AS)

ὀχλέω, -ῶ (ὄχλος), [in LXX: Tob.6:7, 3Ma.5:41 * ;] to move, disturb; hence, generally, to trouble, vex: pass., [[acts 5 6|Act.5:6]] (act. absol., = pass., to be in a tumult, 3Mac, l.with; cf. ἐν-, παρ-εν-οχλέω, and see MM, xviii).† (AS)
ὀχλο-ποιέω, -ῶ to gather a crowd, make a riot: [[acts 17 5|Act.17:5]] (not elsewhere).† (AS)

ὄχλος, -ου, ὁ, [in LXX for הָמוֹן (chiefly in Da TH), קָהָל ,חַיִל, etc. ;] 1. a moving crowd or multitude of persons, a throng: [[matthew 9 23|Mat.9:23]], [[mark 2 4|Mrk.2:4]], [[luke 5 1|Luk.5:1]], [[john 5 13|Jhn.5:13]], al.; pl., [[matthew 5 1|Mat.5:1]], [[mark 10 1|Mrk.10:1]], [[luke 3 7|Luk.3:7]], and freq.; ὄ. ἱκανός, [[mark 10 46|Mrk.10:46]], al.; τοσοῦτος, [[matthew 15 33|Mat.15:33;]] οὐ μετ᾽ ὄχλου, [[acts 24 18|Act.24:18;]] ἄτερ ὄχλου, [[luke 22 6|Luk.22:6;]] πᾶς ὁ ὄ., [[matthew 13 2|Mat.13:2]], [[mark 2 13|Mrk.2:13]], al.; ὄ. πολύς, [[matthew 20 29|Mat.20:29]], [[mark 5 21|Mrk.5:21]], al.; ὁ πολὺς ὄ. (ὄ. π.), the populace, the common people, [[mark 12 37|Mrk.12:37]] (Swete, in l.; Field, Notes, 37), [[john 12 9|Jhn.12:9]] (Westc, in l.). 2. (As also cl., opposite to δῆμος, which see, and cf. Tr., Syn., §xcviii), the populace, the common people (cf. ὁ πολὺς ὄ., supr.), [[matthew 14 5|Mat.14:5 21:26]], [[mark 12 12|Mrk.12:12]], [[john 7 12|Jhn.7:12]]b; so with contempt (cl.), [[john 7 49|Jhn.7:49.]] In a more general sense, a multitude: with genitive, ὀνομάτων (see: ὀ.), [[acts 1 15|Act.1:15;]] μαθητῶν, [[luke 6 17|Luk.6:17]], al. (AS)

ὀχύρωμα, -τος, τό (ὀχυρόω, to fortify, make firm), [in LXX for מִבְצָר, etc. ;] a stronghold, fortress ([[psalms 89 40|Psa.89:40]], [[nahum 3 12|Nam.3:12, 14]] al.); in LXX and NT, also metaphorically of that in which confidence is placed ([[proverbs 10 29|Pro.10:29 21:22]], al.): [[2-corinthians 10 4|2Co.10:4]].† (AS)

ὀψάριον, -ου, τό (dimin. of ὄψον, (1) cooked meat; (2) a relish or dainty, esp. fish, cf. MGr. τὸ ψάρι, fish; in comic poets and late prose writers only) [in LXX: Tob.2:2 א (Β, ὄψον)* ;] fish: [[john 6 9|Jhn.6:9, 11 21:9-10, 13]] † (AS)

ὀψέ, adv. of time [in LXX: [[genesis 24 11|Gen.24:11]], [[exodus 30 8|Exo.30:8]] (עֶרֶב, עֶרֶב בֵּין), [[jeremiah 2 23|Jer.2:23;]] τὸ ὀ., [[isaiah 5 11|Isa.5:11]] (נֶשֶׁף)* ;] 1. long after, late. 2. late in the day, at evening (opposite to πρωί); in late writers used almost as an indecl. noun (see MM, xviii): [[mark 11 11|Mrk.11:11, 19 13:35]]. 3. C. genitive, late in or on; and, in late writers also after (M, Pr., 72 f.), a sense which seems to be required in [[matthew 28 1|Mat.28:1.]]† (AS)

ὄψιμος, -ον (ὀψέ), [in LXX: [[deuteronomy 11 14|Deu.11:14]], [[proverbs 16 15|Pro.16:15]], [[hosea 6 4|Hos.6:4]] (3), [[joel 2 23|Jol.2:23]], [[zechariah 10 1|Zec.10:1]], [[jeremiah 5 24|Jer.5:24]] (מַלְקוֹשׁ), [[exodus 9 32|Exo.9:32]] (אָפִיל)* ;] poët. and late for ὄψιος, late: ὑετὸς ὄ., the latter rain (see DB, see word "rain"), with ellipsis of ὑετός (see WM, 740), Ja 57.† (AS)

ὄψιος, -α, -ον (ὀψέ), late: ἡ ὥρα, [[mark 11 11|Mrk.11:11]] (Rec., WH, mg.). In late writers, ἡ ὀψία (sc. ὥρα), as subst., evening [in LXX: Jdth.13:1*]: [[matthew 8 16|Mat.8:16 14:15, 23 16:2 20:8 26:20 27:57]], [[mark 1 32|Mrk.1:32 4:35 6:47 14:17 15:42]], [[john 6 16|Jhn.6:16 20:10]].† (AS)

ὄψις, -εως, ἡ [in LXX chiefly for מַרְאֶה ;] 1. the act of seeing, the sense of sight. 2. face, countenance: [[john 11 44|Jhn.11:44]], [[revelation 1 16|Rev.1:16]]. 3. appear­ance: κατ᾽ ὄ. κρίνειν (see MM, xviii), [[john 7 24|Jhn.7:24.]]† (AS)
